sections.html:
The loan balance becomes due and payable when the last surviving borrower dies, and no more money can be advanced. On an FHA-insured Home Equity Conversion Mortgage (HECM), the borrower makes no payments while living in the house, and the balance comes due when the borrower sells, stops using it as a primary residence, or dies.

HUD's guidance for heirs allows 30 days from the death to pay off the loan. The lender may approve 90-day extensions when the estate or heirs show they are actively trying to sell the property or repay the loan. The notice rules below start the clock differently, so ask the servicer which deadlines it is applying to your loan.

sections.h2: The notice the lender must send
sections.html:
Under HUD Mortgagee Letter 2022-15, the servicer must send a Due and Payable Notice to the estate, heirs or other party holding legal title within 30 days after it tells HUD the last surviving borrower has died. Earlier guidance started the clock at death.

The notice has to say the estate or heirs may satisfy the loan, sell the property for at least 95 percent of the appraised value, or hand the lender a deed in lieu. Loans with a case number issued before August 4, 2014 where a surviving non-borrowing spouse exists follow earlier letters.

  • Pay the loan balance in full and keep the house.
  • Sell for at least 95 percent of appraised value when the balance is higher than the home's worth.
  • Offer the lender a deed in lieu.

sections.h2: Selling for less than the loan balance
sections.html:
Yes, within HUD's rule. If the balance exceeds the home's value, the estate or heirs may sell for at least 95 percent of the current appraised value, and the lender will accept the net proceeds as payment in full. Any transfer after death counts as a sale for this purpose.

Heirs who want to keep the home must pay off the loan balance in full. Property taxes and insurance stay the responsibility of the borrower's estate until title transfers, so keep paying them while the sale is in motion. Texas property taxes are generally due by January 31, and unpaid bills turn delinquent on February 1 with penalty and interest.

sections.h2: A surviving spouse who is not on the loan
sections.html:
A non-borrowing spouse may qualify for special provisions that postpone repayment and allow the spouse to stay in the home. Among other requirements, the spouse must give the lender a Non-Borrowing Spouse Certification within 30 days of the last surviving borrower's death.

The deadline is short, so call the servicer right away. The FHA Resource Center can be reached at (800) 225-5342, or by email at answers@hud.gov.

sections.h2: Who has authority to sell an inherited home?
sections.html:
That depends on how the owner left the property, and the lender will ask for proof. Several routes can put title in a seller's hands.

Paper that proves authority to sell inherited real property
How the owner left the housePaper recorded or used
Transfer on death deedAffidavit of death and death certificate, recorded
Estate with an executor or administratorExecutor's or administrator's deed
Muniment of titleCourt order and the will
None of the aboveAffidavit of heirship

The county cannot add heirs to the old deed. A will can be probated within four years of the death, and the application normally goes to the court where the person lived. A small estate affidavit is a further option for some estates, with conditions of its own.

sections.h2: What can make a reverse mortgage due early
sections.html:
A reverse mortgage is a loan for homeowners age 62 or older with enough equity, with payment deferred until the borrower dies, sells or moves out. Borrowers still pay property taxes and homeowner's insurance throughout the loan, and interest keeps accruing.

Falling behind on those costs is the usual trigger for a default. Closing costs may be financed into the loan, and the lien is typically paid off when the home is sold. Read the loan documents for the exact default terms, and ask the servicer to list in writing every condition it relies on.

sections.h2: Can the lender foreclose in Texas?
sections.html:
Yes, but a reverse mortgage foreclosure goes through an expedited court order rather than the usual auction by power of sale. Ordinary Texas home loans follow a power-of-sale path with an auction, which is a different track.

After any foreclosure, a buyer facing an occupant may need an eviction case. An heir who plans to sell has more control by listing early than by waiting for the lender to act, since a sale lets the title company pay the lender from proceeds.

sections.h2: Free help with a reverse mortgage
sections.html:
HUD can supply a list of approved reverse mortgage counseling agencies that charge nothing or little. The number is (800) 569-4287. The Homeowner's HOPE Hotline, at (888) 995-4673, is another resource for people facing foreclosure.

  • Lender or servicer: payoff figure, deadlines, extension requests.
  • HUD-approved counselor: options in plain language.
  • Texas attorney: authority to sell, estate issues, disputes.
  • Texas Attorney General: complaints about scams or loan servicing.

Scammers sometimes pass off reverse mortgages as government benefits, so do not sign anything you do not fully understand.

sections.h2: What to gather before you call the servicer
sections.html:
Heirs usually get further on the first call with paper in hand. Have the borrower's death certificate, the loan number, the property address and whatever proof of authority you hold, such as a recorded affidavit of death, an executor's deed or a court order. Write down the date of death, since the 30 day periods run from it or from the servicer's report to HUD.

Then ask for the payoff figure, the appraisal and the extension paperwork in writing, and keep a call log with dates. If the house has to be listed, the title company will order the payoff from the servicer and settle it from the sale money, so the sooner the servicer has your authority documents, the fewer delays you will see at closing.

sections.h2: Questions to ask the servicer before listing
sections.html:
Start with the written payoff figure and the date it expires, since interest keeps accruing on a reverse mortgage. Ask for the appraisal the servicer will use, because the 95 percent measure in HUD's rule is tied to the appraised value, and ask who orders it and when.

  • Which deadline applies to this loan, and when did the 30 days begin?
  • What paperwork shows that an extension is granted, and for how long?
  • Which documents prove my authority to sell?
  • Will the lender accept the net proceeds as full payment if the sale price is under the balance?

Keep the answers in writing. If a servicer will not explain its position, a HUD-approved counselor or the Texas Attorney General's complaint process can help, and the title company handling the closing will pay the lender from the proceeds.

Heirs who would rather not carry the house through a listing can ask whether a cash buyer can close inside the servicer's deadline. A cash sale still has to satisfy the same payoff rules, so get the figures in writing first.

faqs.q: How long do heirs have to pay off a HECM in Texas?
faqs.a: HUD's guidance for heirs allows 30 days from the borrower's death, with 90-day extensions the lender may approve when heirs are actively selling or repaying. Confirm the current deadline with your servicer.

faqs.q: Can I sell for less than the reverse mortgage balance?
faqs.a: Yes, for an FHA-insured HECM. Heirs may sell for at least 95 percent of the current appraised value when the balance is higher, and the lender accepts net proceeds as satisfaction.

faqs.q: Do I owe the difference if the house sells short of the balance?
faqs.a: For a sale at or above 95 percent of appraised value, the lender accepts the net proceeds as satisfaction of the loan. Ask the servicer to confirm that in writing before closing.

faqs.q: What if my spouse was not on the loan?
faqs.a: A non-borrowing spouse may qualify to postpone repayment. A Non-Borrowing Spouse Certification must reach the lender within 30 days of the last borrower's death.

faqs.q: Who pays taxes and insurance after the borrower dies?
faqs.a: The borrower's estate, until title transfers. Unpaid Texas property taxes become delinquent after January 31.
